byCritic.checked: Full surface of app/src: model.ts, state/{useBuddyGraph,useGenerationWorker,useNotice}, io/{importGraph,exportGraph,parseRoster,feasibility,download,readFileText,schema}, worker/{generate.worker,protocol}, graph/{layout,GraphCanvas}, App.tsx and all panels, plus the 22 existing test files and the relevant lib/src/core (bounds, metrics, graph, index) contracts. Ran `npx vitest run` (135 pass). Scratch probes: (1) generation sweep n=3..24, k=2..12 comparing viewFromResult metrics against a recomputed allPairsSummary and comparing isOptimal against the core's asplGap — zero mismatches, zero disconnected outputs; (2) forceLayout determinism and edge-order sensitivity (order-sensitive, max 4.07 unit displacement on a reversed edge list, but export->import provably preserves edge order, so no user-reachable instability); (3) an App-level RTL reroll-after-cancel test that reproduced the finding below. Grepped for Math.random/Date.now/new Date — none. Audited every Set/Map iteration in app/src for order dependence — importGraph sorts adjacency, parseRoster's Maps are insertion-ordered and feed only warning copy, GraphCanvas's highlight sets are membership-only. Checked asplGap's asplLb<=0 escape hatch for a false 100% — unreachable given assembleMetrics' `measurable` gate and MAX_ROSTER=1e6. Checked import boundaries: n=1, n=2, edgeless, self-loops, disconnected, star K1,999, density cap, control chars, parseRoster round-trip gate, settings sanitization/clamping.

Full surface of app/src in .sextant-worktrees/wt-16 (io/{importGraph,exportGraph,parseRoster,download,readFileText,feasibility,schema}, model.ts, App.tsx, state/*, graph/{layout,GraphCanvas}, panels/*, worker/*) plus app/test. Constructed and RAN hostile inputs with vitest+jsdom against the real modules: (a) import fuzzing — oversized people, star n=1000 (degMax 999), max-density 12-regular n=1000, K13, self-loop-only, disconnected, constraints-as-string, settings-as-string, -0 / duplicate / symmetric edges, non-integer & Infinity & NaN buddies/minSeparation/seed, 7MB names, 5MB version object; (b) gate ordering — verified readFileText's 8MB byte gate precedes JSON.parse, and people.length<=1000 + the 2m<=BUDDY_MAX*n density gate both precede new Graph/allPairsSummary/girth/forceLayout (worst-case synchronous re-measure at the cap measured 72-103ms, not a hang); (c) numeric edges at the export boundary — every hostile graph yielded finite quality/largestComponentFraction and null (never Infinity/NaN) for aspl/diameter/girth, and exportGraphJson never emitted null where a number is declared; (d) settings injection — sanitizeSettings clamped a star import's degMax-999 fallback to buddies:12, useBuddyGraph downgraded imported polish:true above POLISH_MAX_N, and I could not drive an out-of-range n/k/minSeparation/seed into the worker; (e) spreadsheet sink, hard — ="cmd|'/C calc'!A0", +1+1, -2+3, @SUM(1), '=x, "=x =y", leading-space " =x", and embedded tab/CR/LF/comma: the leading-only neutralizeCell is SUFFICIENT because parseRoster splits on \n and comma, maps C0+DEL to spaces and trims, and importGraph refuses control chars then requires a parseRoster round-trip, so no name in a GraphView can carry an embedded delimiter; both sinks (toCsv per cell, copyAll per leading name) share the one guard and I could not get an unneutralized formula into either; (f) parseRoster at the 500K char cap — all-duplicates 45ms, 1000-then-duplicates 20ms, one unbroken 500K token 2ms, 250K distinct 0.5ms (early exit), janky per keystroke but bounded; (g) forceLayout caps (FORCE_MAX_N/FORCE_MAX_EDGES) are consistent with the import density cap so no import can exceed them, and the hover second-neighborhood walk is O(m) not O(n^2).

Full-surface read of all 24 files under app/src plus all 22 files under app/test, tracing into the worktree's own lib/ (graph.ts, metrics.ts, bounds.ts, greedy.ts, polish.ts, index.ts) for every number the UI displays. Reproduced with scratch Vitest runs (since deleted; suite left green at 22 files / 135 tests).

Attacked and found clean: (a) DETERMINISM — no Math.random/Date.now in app/src; d3-force's jiggle PRNG is a per-simulation lcg() seeded s=1 (d3-force/src/simulation.js:26), verified forceLayout run-to-run identical; no Set/Map iteration-order dependence reaches a displayed value (importGraph uses g.edgeList() sorted + Array.from(s).sort numeric; GraphCanvas first/second Sets are read only via .has(); parseRoster Maps are insertion-ordered off a deterministic scan). (b) viewFromResult's hardcoded connected:true is actually SOUND, not merely assumed: greedy.ts never calls removeEdge so the ring seed survives, and polish() returns `best`, monotonically non-increasing in penalizedAspl from a connected input (energy < n) while every disconnected graph is >= 10n — so the "disconnected reads as optimal" failure cannot occur on the generation path. (c) IMPORT BOUNDARY — node cap, density cap (2m <= BUDDY_MAX*n, exactly equal to FORCE_MAX_EDGES=6000), settings clamping, parseRoster round-trip, control-char refusal, id-vs-position, constraint refusal, Map-not-object keying (no __proto__ hazard); fuzzed n=1, K2, two triangles, star21, path10, K6+isolate — all scored honestly (quality 0 and aspl null whenever disconnected). (d) ASYNC/STATE — worker id correlation, swapWorker supersession, pending/consumed refs, import-during-in-flight, identical-reroll settings adoption, loadView cancelling a stale run, App's error effect with `view` in deps; walked each interleaving, no clobber or stale-pairing path found. (e) OFF-BY-ONE — MAX_IMPORT_N == MAX_ROSTER_N == MAX_NAMES == 1000 boundary is consistent end-to-end; POLISH_MAX_N=120 matches the core's resolveWantPolish literal; nextRerollSeed wrap; computeFit degenerate spans at n=0/1/2; GraphCanvas's display.length===n render guard covers the one-frame stale-positions window.

Full surface of /home/user/ringweave/.sextant-worktrees/wt-17/app/src (all 27 files) plus app/test. Constructed and RAN hostile inputs through vitest against the real modules: (a) worst-case-legal import at both caps (n=1000, 6000 edges) — measured 100-105 ms synchronous re-measure, acceptable; (b) star import n=1000 with settings.buddies=1 — confirmed sanitizeSettings clamps the 999-degree fallback to BUDDY_MAX=12; (c) force settle at the density cap — 381 ms, bounded by forceIters/FORCE_MAX_EDGES, no hang; (d) spreadsheet sinks: toCsv/neutralizeCell against `=cmd`, leading TAB, `"=1+1`, ` =1+1`, and buddy-cell joins — every cell is RFC4180-quoted so embedded delimiters cannot escape a cell, and the two name producers (parseRoster normalizes C0/DEL to spaces; importGraph refuses C0/DEL outright and enforces a parseRoster round-trip) make an embedded tab/CR/comma/newline unreachable in a name, so the leading-char-only guard is sufficient TODAY; (e) numeric edges: seed=-0, non-integer/NaN/Infinity buddies/minSeparation/seed, version=1.0, self-loops, duplicate edges, mismatched ids, n=1, disconnected imports, degree-1 path graphs — sanitizeInt/clamps hold, no NaN ever reaches quality/qualityPercent, exported metrics are Infinity-free so JSON.stringify cannot corrupt them; (f) parseRoster degenerate inputs (250k duplicate tokens, 1000 distinct long names) — linear, ~50 ms, warning strings bounded; (g) gate ORDER in importGraph — the n cap, density cap and constraints refusal all precede the O(n^2) Graph build and allPairsSummary; (h) prototype-pollution via JSON keys, dangerouslySetInnerHTML/innerHTML/eval — none present; (i) worker protocol, StrictMode worker lifecycle, stale-id dropping, reset/supersede. Two things broke: both are unbounded attacker-controlled STRINGS reaching main-thread layout, not unbounded numbers.

caveats: Recall is a RELATIVE discriminator between configurations, not an absolute capability estimate. Never state "the loop finds N% of defects".
At n~12 a Wilson 95% CI is roughly +/-25 points; existence and zero-loss claims are supportable, effect-size comparisons are not.
Strata are reported separately on purpose: hand-authored seeds are harder to detect than real faults, so cross-stratum comparison is invalid.
Controls measure raw false positives. Whether each is an EFFECTIVE false positive needs adjudication after the run.
